# Update Pro pricing, invite expiry, and Arabic display names

Label: needs-triage

## Problem Statement

Customers are shown an outdated Pro plan price, invitations do not carry an explicit expiry time, and Arabic guest names can be rendered as blank. These behaviors make pricing inaccurate, leave invitation validity ambiguous, and prevent guests with Arabic names from being identified in the guest list.

## Solution

Update the Pro plan price from 12 to 15 while keeping the Team plan at 40. Give every newly created `Invite` an `expires_at` value exactly 14 days after `created_at`, using the same clock-derived creation time as the basis for both timestamps. Make `display_name` preserve Arabic and other Unicode text while continuing to trim surrounding whitespace, enforce its display limit without producing invalid text, and retain the existing presentation behavior for Latin names.

## User Stories

1. As a prospective Pro customer, I want to see the current Pro price of 15, so that I can make a purchase decision using accurate pricing.
2. As a customer purchasing multiple Pro seats, I want each seat to use the updated Pro unit price, so that the calculated total is correct.
3. As a Team customer, I want the Team price to remain 40 per seat, so that the unrelated Pro price change does not alter my pricing.
4. As a user sending an invitation, I want the invitation to record when it was created, so that its validity window has an unambiguous starting point.
5. As a user sending an invitation, I want the invitation to record an explicit expiry time, so that its validity is unambiguous to downstream consumers.
6. As a user sending an invitation, I want the invitation to expire 14 days after creation, so that recipients have the agreed amount of time to act.
7. As a developer consuming an `Invite`, I want `expires_at` to be part of the invite domain object, so that expiry information travels with the invitation rather than being inferred independently.
8. As a developer testing invitation creation, I want creation and expiry to derive from the injected clock, so that the 14-day rule can be verified deterministically.
9. As an Arabic-speaking guest, I want my Arabic name to remain visible in the guest list, so that I can be identified correctly.
10. As a guest whose name contains Unicode characters, I want display shortening to preserve valid characters, so that my displayed name is not blank or corrupted.
11. As a guest, I want surrounding whitespace removed from my displayed name, so that the guest list remains tidy.
12. As a guest with a long name, I want it shortened at a character-safe boundary, so that the display remains compact without malformed text.
13. As a guest with a Latin name, I want the existing title-style presentation to remain intact, so that the current supported behavior does not regress.

## Implementation Decisions

- Modify the pricing domain data so the Pro unit price is 15.
- Keep the Free price at 0 and the Team unit price at 40.
- Continue applying the existing seat multiplication behavior to the updated Pro unit price.
- Extend the `Invite` domain object with an `expires_at` timestamp.
- During invite creation, call the injected clock once for `created_at` and derive `expires_at` by adding 14 days to that exact value. This keeps the timestamps internally consistent and preserves deterministic testing.
- Keep invite expiry calculation encapsulated in invite creation; callers should receive a complete `Invite` rather than calculate expiry themselves.
- Update guest display-name normalization to operate on Unicode characters rather than converting text to ASCII.
- Preserve surrounding-whitespace trimming, the default display limit of 24, and the existing Latin title-style behavior.
- Apply the display limit without splitting an encoded Unicode character. The limit therefore governs displayed characters rather than raw UTF-8 bytes.
- Treat the pricing, invite creation, and display-name changes as independent modules with narrow public interfaces, allowing each behavior to be tested in isolation.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests should assert externally observable results from `price`, `InviteService.create`, and `display_name`; they should not depend on internal constants or implementation steps.
- Extend pricing tests to verify that one Pro seat costs 15 and that multiple Pro seats scale from the updated unit price.
- Retain or add a regression assertion that Team remains 40 per seat, including the existing two-seat total of 80.
- Extend invite creation tests to assert that the returned and stored invite contains the clock value as `created_at` and a timestamp exactly 14 days later as `expires_at`.
- Use the existing injected-clock pattern as prior art for deterministic invite timestamp tests.
- Extend display tests with an Arabic-only name to prove it remains non-blank and readable.
- Add a long Arabic or mixed-Unicode case to prove limiting occurs at valid character boundaries.
- Retain the existing Latin-name test as regression coverage for title-style presentation.
- Include whitespace-trimming coverage where useful to establish that the Unicode fix preserves current normalization behavior.
- The existing application test suite is the prior art for all three areas: it already tests invite storage, Latin display names, and seat-based Team pricing through public interfaces.

## Out of Scope

- Changing the Team plan price; it remains 40.
- Changing the Free plan price.
- Implementing invitation acceptance, rejection, cleanup, renewal, reminder, or expired-invite enforcement flows.
- Defining timezone conversion or persistence behavior beyond preserving the timestamp style already supplied by the invite service clock.
- Redesigning guest-list UI or changing the default display-name limit.
- Coding or shipping these changes as part of this handoff.

## Further Notes

- The initial seven-day invitation lifetime was superseded by the final decision of 14 days.
- The proposed Team price change to 45 was withdrawn; 40 is the explicit retained value.
- This PRD records the decisions for a fresh implementation session and intentionally contains no implementation changes.
